blockingFindings: Verification evidence is not bound to the reviewed head c403c1674d01450a072ed3bda556d95d21f5d361. The Markdown names implementation head 27505c85fd3506f5178c85477fe0e3a6c069c54f, the JSON predates subsequent revisions, and both report 16 review-runner checks while the committed test declares 21. These stale and contradictory records cannot establish final-head verification.

Windows cancellation does not reliably satisfy the child-tree isolation requirement. child.kill(SIGINT or SIGTERM) can terminate the direct process immediately, causing close handling to cancel the escalation timer before descendants are terminated; this can recreate the orphaned-child condition the task is intended to repair. Conversely, delayed PID-based taskkill has no exited-process or PID-reuse guard and could target an unrelated process.

The newly added merge-risk context construction has no deterministic coverage in the supplied diff. Tests do not establish canonical base/head selection, changed-path and diff inclusion, Git failure handling, context-budget enforcement, sensitive-material rejection, or behavior when origin/main and the reviewed head have diverged.
nonBlockingRisks: The generated merge-risk material is derived from bound base and head SHAs but is not itself represented by an entry or hash in contextManifest, reducing direct auditability of the exact generated bytes reviewed.

Using the three-dot diff range derives changes from the merge base rather than literally comparing the recorded canonical base commit with the reviewed head; the intended merge-scope semantics should be documented and tested.
The launcher continues to combine authorization, context generation, process lifecycle, trace emission, assessment validation, and persistence, so future changes retain broad regression coupling.
missingNegativeTests: Exercise real or platform-faithful Windows cancellation for both SIGINT and SIGTERM and prove descendants cannot remain orphaned after the direct child exits.

Exercise cancellation after child exit, delayed stream close, repeated signals, PID reuse, and an unrelated sibling process; assert only the launched process tree is affected, exactly one cancelled terminal event is emitted, and no review artifact is persisted.

Test merge-risk context generation when origin/main is not an ancestor of HEAD, when Git diff fails, when generated content exceeds the packet context budget, and when the generated diff contains sensitive material.
Assert the generated merge-risk context contains the exact intended changed-path set and diff for its bound base and head and cannot silently switch revisions during context construction.

architectureAssessment.deepModules: The repair remains concentrated in the existing launcher and task-validation modules, but launch.mjs is a broad orchestration module whose routing, context, process-control, tracing, validation, and persistence responsibilities amplify regression impact.
architectureAssessment.hexagonalArchitecture: No production, provider-fallback, deployment, package, schema, or P3-001 boundary is widened, and repository validation remains separate from the Codex process adapter; the unresolved Windows process-tree behavior nevertheless violates the intended local adapter isolation.
architectureAssessment.eventedBoundaries: Structured redacted progress and singular terminal-state control are present, but the direct-child close and escalation-timer interaction does not reliably model the lifetime of the complete child tree on Windows.

exactNextAction: Return GOV-057 to revision-required; implement platform-safe process-tree cancellation with exited-process and PID-reuse protection, add deterministic merge-risk-context and Windows cancellation race coverage, then rerun every packet-listed check on a new committed head and replace the stale verification records with exact-head evidence and correct check counts before requesting fresh SHA-bound plan, semantic, and merge-risk reviews.
